bib.title: Reasoning or Reciting? Exploring the Capabilities and Limitations of Language Models Through Counterfactual Tasks

question: Do LM successes on standard tasks come from general, transferable reasoning or from narrow procedures tied to default conditions seen in pretraining?
hypothesis: If models implement general task-solving procedures they perform comparably on default and counterfactual task variants; if they rely on default-specific procedures, counterfactual performance drops.
contributions: A counterfactual evaluation framework that changes the world model (e.g. number base) while keeping the reasoning procedure fixed, with counterfactual comprehension checks (CCCs)
A suite of 11 tasks across arithmetic, code, syntax, logic, spatial reasoning, drawing, music, chess and SET
Analysis of commonness, proximity, default-counterfactual correlation and prompting effects

method.summary: Four LMs are evaluated zero-shot on 11 tasks in default and counterfactual world variants, with and without zero-shot CoT, plus a task-specific counterfactual comprehension check to separate misunderstanding the prompt from failing the task.

other.use: 0-shot 100-way classification of drawings; agrees with humans 84% of 240 images

inference.decoding: temperature 0 by default; HumanEval generation uses temperature 0.1 for pass@1 and 0.8 for pass@10
inference.temperature: 0 (0.1/0.8 for HumanEval generation; 0.1 for chess CCC)
inference.samples: 1 greedy sample per item; HumanEval 50 samples; chess CCC 15 samples per piece at temperature 0.1
inference.prompting: 0-shot, with and without 'Let's think step by step' (0-CoT); no system message; few-shot CoT (up to 16 demos) for arithmetic analysis only

parameters.counterfactual_comprehension_check: simpler control task with the same world-model prompt

other.palm2_exclusions: PaLM-2 omitted from code execution and drawing due to 1,024 output limit

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction correct per task; spatial requires all 3 objects correct

metrics.name: human-judged drawing accuracy
metrics.definition: 4 annotators decide if drawing matches object including canonical orientation

baselines: default-condition performance of the same model
eval.protocol: Compare default vs counterfactual accuracy per model, with and without 0-CoT; no seeds or significance tests reported except bootstrap CIs in the FOLIO regression.

availability.data: synthetic data and LM interactions released, except FOLIO interactions (non-public)

prompts.text: You are a mathematician. Assuming that all numbers are in base-11 where the digits are "0123456789A", what is 59+37? {Let’s think step by step, and }end the response with the result in "\boxed{result}".

You are an expert programmer who can readily adapt to new programming languages. There is a new programming language, ThonPy, which is identical to Python 3.7 except all variables of the `list`, `tuple`, and `str` types use 1-based indexing ...
You are playing a chess variant where the starting positions for knights and bishops are swapped.

limits: Counterfactual difficulty may differ from default (e.g. base-11 has an extra digit; melody in another key may need a two-step transposition), so gaps may be underestimates of overfitting or reflect difficulty (Limitations)
Counterfactual conditions may appear in pretraining, so gaps could be larger for truly unseen conditions
Some perturbations admit a shortcut mapping back to default (logic word replacement, drawing transforms), plausibly explaining high logic counterfactual performance
CCC is heuristic and a nonperfect CCC cannot cleanly separate comprehension failure from task failure
FOLIO subset is 81 instances; no seeds, one greedy run per item; PaLM-2 was not the largest model; models are 2023 API snapshots
Authors claim a perfect prompt cannot be ruled out; few-shot demos shrink but do not close the gap

terms.definition: Task variant that deviates from the default conditions assumed in standard tasks while keeping the same reasoning procedure
A simpler control task that tests whether the LM understands the specified counterfactual world
